title: Land Cruiser Prado 90
verdict: The Land Cruiser America wasn't allowed to have: a 3rd-gen 4Runner's bones under a full-time-4WD Land Cruiser badge, with a diesel the US never got. Now that the calendar has done its work, it's the most affordable way to park a real JDM Land Cruiser in your driveway. Just keep that diesel cool.

paragraphs: On 8 May 1996 Toyota launched a Land Cruiser that most Americans have never seen in the metal. The second-generation Prado, the J90, was the mid-size Land Cruiser: a ladder-frame wagon with full-time four-wheel drive, coil springs at both ends, and the independent front suspension it shared with the Hilux Surf, the truck North America bought as the [[4runner/3rd-gen|3rd-gen 4Runner]]. It went on sale in Japan, Australia, Britain and Latin America, but never in the United States. That held for a quarter of a century, until the 25-year import rule started letting them in.

story.heading: A LAND CRUISER FOR PEOPLE
paragraphs: The first Prado had been a lighter-duty offshoot of the [[land-cruiser/70-series|70 Series]]. Toyota made the J90 a series of its own and, in its own words, pointed it toward a more passenger-oriented four-wheel drive. There were two bodies: a three-door, five-seat short wheelbase on 2,370 mm and a five-door, eight-seat long wheelbase on 2,675 mm. Toyota gave the short one a sportier face and the long one a more rugged one. The drivetrain switched from part-time to full-time 4WD, and the suspension (double wishbones at the front, a four-link coil-sprung axle with a lateral rod at the back) was the same as the Hilux Surf's. 'Prado', Toyota notes, is Portuguese for a meadow or field.

story.heading: FOUR ENGINES AND NO V8
paragraphs: At launch you had a choice of two engines. The new one was the 3.4-liter 5VZ-FE V6 with 185 PS, the same family of V6 Americans got in the 4Runner. The carry-over was the 3.0-liter 1KZ-TE four-cylinder turbo-diesel, which gained an intercooler and 140 PS. A 2.7-liter 3RZ-FE four with 150 PS followed in April 1997. In July 2000 Toyota replaced the 1KZ-TE in Japan with the 1KD-FTV, its new common-rail D-4D: 170 PS and 352 Nm, and the first vehicle that engine ever went into.

Market by market, the line-up varied. Australia launched the Prado in July 1996 with petrol engines only and didn't get a diesel until March 2000, when the 96 kW 1KZ-TE arrived with a five-speed manual; an automatic followed that October. 4X4 Australia's buyer's guide, written with hindsight, advises steering clear of the 2.7 four. Britain called the truck the Land Cruiser Colorado, to tell it apart from the bigger 'Amazon', and Venezuela sold the three-door as the Toyota Merú.

story.heading: THE 1999 FACELIFT
paragraphs: Toyota gave the J90 its minor change on 9 June 1999. Both bodies got big multi-reflector headlights and clear-lens lamps front and rear, plus a new grille, bumper, door trim and instruments, including a newly offered Optitron cluster and a Field Monitor display that switched to color. Underneath, Toyota added 'Active TRC' traction control for loose and muddy surfaces, and from August 1999 vehicle stability control on the main automatic grades. A TX Limited special edition arrived at the same time with roof rails, wood-grain trim and the Optitron gauges. Five-door trucks grew slightly, to 4,690 mm long.

story.heading: WHY AMERICANS ARE BUYING THEM NOW
paragraphs: The J90 was replaced in October 2002 by the [[land-cruiser/prado-120|Prado 120]], although Sofasa kept assembling it in Colombia until 2009. In the US it stayed off-limits until each truck turned 25, counted from its month of manufacture, so the first J90s became legal imports in 2021. In January 2022 IH8MUD started a 90 Series FAQ because 'Prado 90's [were] finally available for US import'. By 2026 Bring a Trailer had a model page for them, and most of the trucks sold there went for $10,000 to $16,000.

Living with one in America is easier than you'd think. The front suspension and plenty of hardware are shared with the 3rd-gen 4Runner. IH8MUD members have fitted 4Runner front rotors (Toyota 43512-35210), the rear rotors match the [[land-cruiser/80-series|80 Series]], and US Land Cruiser specialists now stock 9x Prado ball joints, brakes and axle kits. The rest is a job for a Japanese parts catalogue and a VIN or frame number. Just remember the Prado has rear discs where many 4Runners have drums, and that its rear axle shafts have a different bolt pattern.

callout.label: SIDEBAR · THE PRADO ON TRACKS
callout.title: The 1999 Prado Crawler
paragraphs: On 22 October 1999 Toyota announced a factory 'Crawler' version of the Prado (and a matching Hilux Surf) through its TECS special-vehicle program. It went on sale on 1 November. Each road wheel was replaced by a triangular, rubber-belted crawler unit, turning a 3.4 V6 TZ into a snow vehicle for passengers and cargo. Araco built the bodies, and the crawler units could be swapped back for wheels outside the snow season.

Because the controls were unchanged, Toyota said the Crawler could be driven on an ordinary Japanese licence, unlike purpose-built tracked snow vehicles. The tracks added 440 kg (2,420 kg against the donor's 1,980 kg) and raised ground clearance from 230 mm to 330 mm. A speedometer switch corrected the reading between tracks and wheels. Launch price was ¥5,240,000 before tax.

engineering_intro: The J90 is a body-on-frame wagon with double-wishbone independent front suspension and a four-link, coil-sprung live rear axle with a lateral rod, the same layout as the Hilux Surf and 3rd-gen 4Runner. Unlike those trucks, every Prado has full-time four-wheel drive with a lockable center differential. Wheels are 6 on 139.7 mm with M12 x 1.5 nuts.

engineering.v: Ladder frame; 2,675 mm (105.3 in) 5-door, 2,370 mm (93.3 in) 3-door

engineering.note: Shared with the Hilux Surf/4Runner, so 4Runner shocks and lift parts bolt on.

engineering.v: Live axle, four links, lateral rod, coils
engineering.note: Semi-floating, with disc brakes. Shaft bolt pattern differs from the 4Runner's.
Some manual trucks lock the center diff automatically when you select low range.

engineering.v: No factory axle lockers in Australia
engineering.note: Center lock only; owners add ARB Air Lockers.
The 1KD-FTV common-rail diesel replaced the 1KZ-TE in Japan in July 2000.

generations_table.note: Launch petrol engine. Belt-driven cams, non-interference.
Added in April 1997. Timing chain. 4X4 Australia says to skip it.
Intercooled, indirect injection. Australia got it only from March 2000 (96 kW).
From July 2000; the first application of the 1KD.
Built in Colombia largely unchanged: three-door 2.7 and five-door V6.

buying_checks.head: Ask when the lower ball joints were done
buying_checks.body: Australia recalled a range of five-door Prados in May 2005 (PRA 2005/7749) because a scratched joint could wear and separate from the knuckle. AustralianCar.Reviews says joints still fail after the recall, and IH8MUD owners replace them preventively with genuine Toyota parts, because a joint can feel tight and still let go.

buying_checks.head: Diesel: hunt for signs of overheating
buying_checks.body: On the 1KZ-TE, overheating is how heads crack. Look for coolant bubbling into the overflow bottle, coolant loss or discoloration, and a gauge that climbs on hills or in traffic. Known causes include a tired viscous fan hub, a blocked radiator and a seized wastegate actuator. On a 260,000 km truck, one IH8MUD member's verdict was that 'the head on the 1kz has already been done', so ask for the receipt.

buying_checks.head: Check the ATF for coolant
buying_checks.body: The automatic's oil cooler sits inside the engine radiator, so a crack lets coolant into the transmission. Pink, milky fluid on the dipstick is a deal-breaker, or at least a new radiator and a transmission rebuild.

buying_checks.head: Rear axle flange recall (early trucks)
buying_checks.body: Prados built from 17 April 1996 to 6 January 1999 were recalled in Australia (PRA 2006/8499) because the rear axle-shaft flange could crack after repeated hard driving on winding roads, and in the worst case let the wheel come off. A Japanese import won't have the paperwork, so inspect the flanges.

buying_checks.head: Know which engine you're buying
buying_checks.body: The model code tells you: VZJ = 3.4 V6, RZJ = 2.7 four, KZJ = 1KZ-TE diesel, KDJ = 1KD-FTV diesel (July 2000 on, Japan). '90' is the three-door, '95' the five-door. The V6 has a timing belt, and the 2.7 a chain.

buying_checks.head: Timing belt history
buying_checks.body: HD Automotive gives the 1KZ-TE belt interval as 100,000 km or 5–6 years, and the 5VZ-FE V6 is a 90,000-mile belt. With no receipt, budget for the belt and water pump on day one.

buying_checks.head: Import paperwork
buying_checks.body: A US truck should come with proof that it was at least 25 years old on entry (the date runs from manufacture), the customs entry and the NHTSA HS-7 and EPA 3520-1 declarations. Check that your state will title and register it before you buy, especially California.

buying_checks.head: Test the sub tank and CV boots
buying_checks.body: On trucks with a sub tank, check that the switch-over works: AustralianCar.Reviews warns the mechanism can seize and the fuel go stale if it was never used. While you're underneath, look for split CV boots and grease on the inside of the front wheels.

repairs.title: Replace the front lower ball joints
repairs.time: ≈ Half a day for both sides
repairs.cost: Parts only; buy genuine Toyota, as IH8MUD owners report early failures with cheap aftermarket joints
repairs.symptoms: Heavy steering, poor self-centring, vibration or shudder in turns, a torn boot, or simply no record that they've ever been changed. A worn joint can let go without warning.
repairs.fix: Support the truck on stands, remove the wheel and take the load off the lower arm. Remove the castle nut and split the taper from the lower control arm, then unbolt the four bolts that hold the ball joint to the back of the knuckle and fit the new joint. Toyota superseded the original 43340-39325 / 43330-39415 joints to 43340-39465 (left) and 43330-39585 (right). One IH8MUD owner's ball-joint bolts worked loose, and he blamed the anti-seize he'd put on the threads, so torque them per the factory manual and use thread-locker, not anti-seize. Finish with an alignment.
repairs.tools: Floor jack and stands · 14/19/24 mm sockets · ball-joint separator · torque wrench · thread-locker · new cotter pins · eight knuckle bolts 90105-10406 (per ToyoDIY, quoted on IH8MUD)

repairs.title: 1KZ-TE timing belt and water pump
repairs.time: HD Automotive says labor is often quoted at around an hour for the belt
repairs.cost: HD Automotive's 1KZ belt kit lists at AUD $246; its 'major front service kit' adds the water pump and fan belts
repairs.symptoms: No warning; it's on a schedule. HD Automotive quotes 100,000 km or 5–6 years, Roughtrax's UK sheet 60,000 miles or 60 months.
repairs.fix: Drain the coolant and remove the fan and shroud, drive belts, crank pulley and timing covers. Line up the timing marks, then replace the belt, tensioner pulley and hydraulic tensioner, plus the cam, crank and injection-pump seals. If you do the water pump at the same time, as HD Automotive recommends, fit a new gasket and refill with Toyota long-life coolant. Rotate the engine by hand twice and recheck the marks before you button it up.
repairs.tools: Metric sockets · crank-pulley holder and puller · seal puller · torque wrench · factory manual or Gregory's 1KZ-TE manual for torques and timing marks

parts.name: Timing belt kit for 1KZ Hilux/Prado (belt, tensioner pulley, hydraulic tensioner, seals)
Major front service kit for 1KZ, Prado KZJ90/KZJ120 (adds water pump and fan belts)

repairs.title: Cooling-system overhaul on a 1KZ-TE (save the head)
repairs.time: ≈ A day if you do the hoses and fan hub too
repairs.cost: A Koyorad KZJ95 automatic radiator lists at AUD $379 at HD Automotive; one IH8MUD owner paid AUD $200 for a Koyo locally
repairs.symptoms: The temperature gauge climbs on hills, while towing or in hot traffic; coolant smells, or the level keeps dropping. AustralianCar.Reviews says overheating on this engine 'requires urgent attention' because it cracks heads.
repairs.fix: Replace the radiator with an OEM-spec unit, not a cheap aluminum one. IH8MUD members tried one that didn't fit the mounts or take the factory cap. On automatics, keep the trans cooler in the new radiator. Replace the radiator and heater hoses and, as one owner learned, the small coolant hoses to the turbo. Check the viscous fan hub (a weak hub shows up as heat in traffic) and that the wastegate actuator moves freely. Refill and bleed with Toyota long-life coolant.
repairs.tools: Drain pan · hose-clamp pliers · 10/12 mm sockets · coolant funnel · Toyota red or blue long-life coolant

parts.name: Upgraded viscous hub and 10-blade fan, 1KZ-TE KZJ90/KZJ120

repairs.title: Replace a cracked 1KZ-TE cylinder head
repairs.time: ≈ A weekend for a capable home mechanic
repairs.cost: Parts plus a head; AustralianCar.Reviews recommends a genuine Toyota head because some non-genuine heads have had casting faults
repairs.symptoms: Bubbles or coolant pushing into the overflow bottle, coolant loss, rapid overheating, rough running and lost power. A pressure test may not show the crack.
repairs.fix: Fix whatever made it overheat first (radiator, fan hub, wastegate, hoses), or the new head will crack too. Remove the timing belt, intake and exhaust, injector lines and turbo oil and coolant lines, then the head. Have the block deck checked, fit a genuine head gasket, and reassemble with a fresh timing belt. An IH8MUD member's 'lessons learned' thread is a reminder to put the washers back under the head bolts.
repairs.tools: Full metric socket set · torque wrench and angle gauge · straight-edge and feeler gauges · factory or Gregory's manual for the head-bolt sequence

parts.name: Timing belt kit for 1KZ (do it while it's apart)

repairs.title: 5VZ-FE timing belt and water pump (V6 trucks)
repairs.time: ≈ 8–14 hours the first time (AdventureTaco, on the same engine in a Tacoma)
repairs.symptoms: None until it snaps. The 5VZ-FE is non-interference, so a broken belt strands you but shouldn't bend valves. Plan on about 90,000 miles.
repairs.fix: It's the same job as on a 3rd-gen 4Runner. Drain the coolant, remove the fan, shroud and drive belts, then the upper timing covers. Hold the crank pulley, break the bolt, pull the pulley and lower cover, and set cylinder 1 to TDC. Replace the belt, idlers, hydraulic tensioner, cam and crank seals, water pump and thermostat. Rotate the engine twice to confirm the marks, then torque the new crank bolt. The 4Runner part numbers below are the common ones, but check them against your Prado's frame number in an EPC.
repairs.tools: Harmonic-balancer holder · puller · cam-pulley holder · seal puller · torque wrench · new crank bolt

parts.name: Toyota timing belt 13568-69095 (5VZ-FE; confirm by frame number)

repairs.title: Rebuild the rear axle seals and bearings
repairs.cost: Seals, bearings and retainers; Cruiser Outfitters sells a complete kit
repairs.symptoms: Gear oil on the inside of the rear wheel or brakes, a low diff level, or a clunk in reverse after the diff has run low.
repairs.fix: Drain the diff, remove the wheel and rear brake, unbolt the axle-shaft retainer and pull the shaft. Replace the inner seal in the housing. Once a seal has leaked, the bearing's grease has usually washed out, so IH8MUD members replace the bearing too, which means pressing it and its retainer collar off and on. If the seal is the same superseded part as on a 3rd-gen 4Runner, look up the 'retainer flip' method: the new seal sits further inboard. Refit with new gaskets and O-rings and refill the diff.
repairs.tools: Slide hammer or axle puller · 20-ton press · seal driver · torque wrench · gear oil

parts.name: Rear axle overhaul kit, major, 1990–2002 KZJ/RZJ/VZJ9x semi-float (RAKLJ7X9X)

repairs.title: Front pads and rotors, using 4Runner interchange
repairs.cost: Pads and rotors; IH8MUD members source them in the US
repairs.symptoms: Pulsing pedal, grooved or thin rotors, squealing pads.
repairs.fix: IH8MUD's 90 Series FAQ confirms the front rotor is Toyota 43512-35210, as used on 1995–2002 V6 4Runners and Tacomas. Make sure you get the larger V6 rotor, because four-cylinder 4Runners used a smaller one that won't fit. Members list the rear rotors as 42431-60200/-60201, the same as the 80 Series. Remove the caliper, hang it, swap the rotor and pads, clean and grease the slides, and bed in the pads.
repairs.tools: Metric sockets · C-clamp or piston tool · brake cleaner · high-temperature grease · torque wrench

repairs.title: Diagnose a sub tank that won't switch
repairs.symptoms: You flick the sub-tank switch, the sub-tank light comes on, but the main-tank gauge keeps falling.
repairs.fix: On the 1KZ-TE, the lift pump is part of the injection pump, so the lines between tank and pump are under vacuum. An IH8MUD member suggests starting at the fuel-tank switch-over valve (he found it listed as Toyota 77710-60040): check that it gets power when you flick the switch, and that it actually changes over. AustralianCar.Reviews warns that a sub tank that was never used can seize its switching mechanism and leave stale fuel behind, so drain old fuel before you trust it.
repairs.tools: Multimeter · wiring diagram for your engine (petrol and diesel circuits differ) · fuel-safe catch can

parts.name: Toyota fuel tank switch-over valve 77710-60040 (confirm by frame number)

faq.q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
faq.a: 265/75R16 (about 31.6 in). An IH8MUD member who has owned both a 90 and a 95 says it won't rub on stock suspension unless the springs have sagged, and ExplorOz members add that it needs the 7-inch rims of a GXL-type truck, because it's too wide for the 6-inch rims on base models. 285/75R16 rubs with or without a lift, on the upper control arm and a rear pinch weld. For 33s, the same IH8MUD member suggests a lift and 255/85R16s.

faq.q: Can I legally import and register one in the US?
faq.a: Yes, once it's 25 years old. NHTSA lets a vehicle at least 25 years old in without meeting US safety standards, counting from its date of manufacture, and EPA exempts vehicles at least 21 years old in original configuration. J90 production began in 1996, so the first trucks qualified in 2021, and the last 2002 builds qualify during 2027. Titling and emissions are up to your state, and California is the hardest.

Under the skin, nearly. Toyota says the Prado and Hilux Surf (the 4Runner) shared their suspension: double wishbones at the front and a four-link coil rear axle. 4Runner shocks, front rotors and lift kits bolt on. The differences that matter: every Prado has full-time 4WD, it has rear disc brakes, it has a different body, and it offers diesels the 4Runner never got in the US.

The 1KZ-TE diesel is simple but cracks heads if it overheats. The 1KD-FTV (Japan, July 2000 on) has 170 PS and a 16-valve head that an IH8MUD member says is far less crack-prone, but its common-rail injectors cost much more to replace. The 3.4 V6 is the 4Runner's proven 5VZ-FE. 4X4 Australia's advice is to avoid the 2.7 four.

Every J90 has full-time 4WD with a center-diff lock. ExplorOz members say Australian J90s had no factory front or rear axle lockers. On some manual trucks the center diff locks mechanically whenever you select low range, while others have a dash switch. ARB Air Lockers are the usual retrofit.

faq.q: When is the timing belt due?
faq.a: HD Automotive gives the 1KZ-TE belt as 100,000 km or 5–6 years (Roughtrax's UK schedule says 60,000 miles or 60 months). The 5VZ-FE V6 belt is about 90,000 miles, and that engine is non-interference. The 2.7 3RZ-FE has a timing chain.

faq.q: What fluids and capacities does a KZJ95 take?
faq.a: Per Roughtrax's KZJ90/95 sheet: engine oil 7.7 L with filter (5W-40, API CF); coolant 9.5 L, or 11 L with a rear heater; manual gearbox 2.2 L and transfer case 1.2 L of 75W-90 GL-4/5; front diff 1.1 L and rear 2.9 L (2.6 L of LSD oil if you have an LSD); automatic 3.0 L per drain-and-fill; power steering 0.8 L of Dexron II/III. Confirm against your manual.

Prado-specific kits exist: Dobinsons sells an IMS kit for the Prado 90/95, and an IH8MUD member notes Ironman made one too. Because the front end is the same as a 3rd-gen 4Runner's, 4Runner kits fit. One owner found a 2.5 in OME 4Runner kit gave about 3.5 in on his 90, and he needed a diff drop and stronger front axles. Above 2–3 in, members warn, the CV joints suffer.

faq.q: Where do I get parts in the US?
faq.a: Many wear parts cross over from 3rd-gen 4Runners and Tacomas. For the rest, IH8MUD members look up genuine part numbers by frame number in an online EPC such as Partsouq, Amayama or ToyoDIY. Cruiser Outfitters (CruiserTeq) in Utah stocks 9x Prado ball joints, brakes and axle kits.

On Bring a Trailer, 19 J90s sold between December 2024 and October 2026, mostly for $10,000–$16,000. The extremes were $9,500 for a 1996 KZJ90 and $34,500 for a 1997 KZJ90. Diesels dominate the listings.

mods.why: Fresh springs and shocks undo 25 years of sag. Diesels need heavier front springs than V6 trucks, and Dobinsons makes a Prado-95 diesel setup for exactly that.

mods.why: There isn't much aftermarket armor for the 90 in the US, which is why Coastal Offroad's weld-together kits come up on IH8MUD. One owner warns that their rear bumper only fits five-doors.

baseline_service.intro: Assume a 25-year-old import has had nothing done, whatever the auction sheet says. On a diesel the priorities are the timing belt and the cooling system, because heat is what kills a 1KZ-TE head. Specs below are from Roughtrax's KZJ90/95 data sheet unless noted. V6 and 2.7 petrols differ, so confirm in the manual for your engine.

items.spec: 1KZ-TE: 7.7 L with filter, SAE 5W-40, API SL/CF · petrol engines [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]
items.interval: Every 6,000 mi or 12 months (6 months in severe use)
items.note: Roughtrax's UK schedule. Replace the sump-plug washer every time.

items.interval: Inspect at every oil change; more often on dusty trails
items.note: A diesel that breathes dust wears fast. Check the airbox seals too.

items.spec: Diesel filter with water separator [CONFIRM PART BY FRAME NUMBER]
items.note: Drain the water trap whenever the warning light comes on, and after filling from a questionable source.

items.spec: 1KZ-TE: belt, tensioner pulley, hydraulic tensioner, seals · 5VZ-FE: belt 13568-69095 (4Runner part) · 3RZ-FE: chain
items.interval: 1KZ-TE: 100,000 km or 5–6 years (HD Automotive); Roughtrax says 60,000 mi or 60 months · 5VZ-FE: about 90,000 mi
items.note: If there's no receipt, do it now and replace the water pump at the same time.

parts.name: Major front service kit, 1KZ (belt, tensioners, seals, water pump)

items.spec: 9.5 L (11 L with rear heater) · Toyota red or blue Long Life Coolant
items.note: On a 1KZ-TE, also replace the small turbo coolant hoses and check the viscous fan hub. The automatic's cooler is inside the radiator, so a leak here can contaminate the ATF.

items.spec: 3.0 L per drain-and-fill, 10.1 L dry · Dexron II/III or Toyota T-IV (Roughtrax lists these as guidance only)
items.interval: Then per the owner's manual [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]
items.note: Look for pink, milky fluid (coolant from the radiator cooler) before you do anything else. Do repeated drain-and-fills rather than one flush.

items.spec: 75W-90 GL-4/5 · front 1.1 L · rear 2.9 L (open or locker), or 2.6 L of LSD-rated hypoid oil if you have an LSD
items.interval: Front every 36,000 mi · rear every 18,000 mi
items.note: If the rear has run low it can clunk in reverse. Check the inner axle seals while you're there.
An IH8MUD member notes Toyota sells a pump seal kit (04446-60091) for the diesel's power-steering pump.

items.interval: Brakes every 18,000 mi · clutch every 24,000 mi
items.note: Rear discs on every Prado. Front rotors are the 4Runner V6 part 43512-35210.

items.interval: Every 6,000 mi or 6 months (3,000 mi or 3 months in severe use)
items.note: Grease the U-joints and slip yokes.

items.note: Replace any joint with play or a torn boot, and replace them anyway if there's no record. Toyota's split CV-boot kit can be fitted without removing the driveshaft.
